description:
About the Position

This Wageningen postdoctoral position examines governance arrangements that support sustainability transitions in farming systems. The work is hosted by Animal Production Systems and includes research connected to ReGeNL. Wageningen University & Research invites applications for a postdoctoral position in this area: Governance and Sustainability Transitions in Farming Systems at Wageningen, Netherlands. Research areas covered include Governance, Public Policy, Environmental Science. The host institution is in Wageningen, Netherlands. According to the listing, funding covers the full cost of participation; financial support is listed as €3,706–€5,760 gross per month for a 38-hour working week.. The stated deadline is 15 November 2026.

Research Position Overview

Study public and private governance, certification, standards and sustainability indicators. Work with stakeholders on regenerative agriculture, contribute to policy-oriented projects and proposals, and take part in education where relevant. This postdoctoral opening at Wageningen University & Research centres on Governance and Sustainability Transitions in Farming Systems at Wageningen, Netherlands. Research areas covered include Governance, Public Policy, Environmental Science. The host institution is in Wageningen, Netherlands. Full funding is provided; financial support is listed as €3,706–€5,760 gross per month for a 38-hour working week.. Interested candidates should note the deadline: 15 November 2026.

Research Areas

  • Regenerative agriculture
  • Farming governance
  • Sustainability indicators

  • Application deadline: 15 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.

  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

  • Provide a motivation letter through the official application system.

Submit through the application system linked from the official vacancy. Follow its current document and translation instructions.

Research contact: Evelien de Olde.
